g.text: How high each US policy tool stands at each stage of three supply chains, ranked against the
same tool across all US imports: High = top 10% of traded products, Medium = next 30%, Low =
the rest. At assembly, tariffs rank Low or Medium while domestic-market rules (local content,
public purchasing) rank High in all three chains.
America's new trade regime is not really just a tariff
† The band rests on a single NIPO measure. Red triangle: from 4 December 2026 a Section 232 minimum import price and 15% tariff
(Proclamation 11052) also apply to polysilicon, wafers, cells and modules; they are not in the tariff band, which uses August
Tariffs: rank of the stage's import-weighted applied rate. Other tools: import-weighted mean percentile of the stage's products
by the number of NIPO measures in force on 31 October 2026 naming each HS6 code; measures naming over 500 codes (sanctions
lists) are excluded and trade-defence scopes are checked against the orders. A measure named on a product may bite on part of
its trade only (one firm, partner or end use).
Assembly and Deployment share one basket. Sources: Global Trade Alert New Industrial Policy Observatory (October 2026 extract);
